state_space: Two declared system alternatives x in {0,delta} with nonnegative integer separation delta, plus one finite environment cell e in {0,...,d-1} at positive integer record resolution d.
transition_law: The candidate environment record is generated deterministically by record_d(x,e)=floor((e+x)/d), implemented by exact integer division. The environment microstate is taken uniformly over the declared d-state cell only inside this toy subfamily.
observation_map: The two alternatives have exact finite record overlap eta=max(d-delta,0)/d because exactly max(d-delta,0) of the d environment microstates produce equal records. The declared visibility premodel remains V_predicted=eta*V_ordinary with 0<=V_ordinary<=1.

parameters.name: d
parameters.prior_allowed_region: positive integers fixed independently for a declared apparatus/environment configuration

parameters.name: delta
parameters.prior_allowed_region: nonnegative integers fixed independently for the two declared alternatives

symmetries.name: translation within one declared quotient-record coordinate
symmetries.residual_observable: Only the finite quotient record is defined. No spatial Lorentz/rotation/translation symmetry of a physical universe is claimed by this toy record generator.

predictions.observable: matter-wave fringe visibility relative to the declared ordinary-quantum/environment baseline
predictions.unavoidable_prediction: For predeclared integer d and delta, eta=max(d-delta,0)/d and V_predicted=eta*V_ordinary with 0<=V_ordinary<=1, so V_predicted<=max(d-delta,0)/d.
predictions.current_constraint: Pedalino et al. (Nature 2026) report representative sodium-nanoparticle matter-wave visibility V=0.10 +/- 0.01 in the stated high-mass regime. R004 reads only the published numerical range [0.09,0.11] for this algebraic toy comparison.
predictions.excluded_parameter_region: For the representative numerical range, every predeclared pair (d,delta) with eta<0.09 is algebraically unable to reach the observed lower endpoint. Equivalently, because d>0, the exact integer condition is 100*delta>91*d. This is not a confidence-level/full-likelihood exclusion and does not calibrate d or delta to the real apparatus.
predictions.falsified_if: For an independently calibrated apparatus-to-(d,delta) map, the experimentally allowed visibility interval is disjoint from [0,max(d-delta,0)/d] times the independently calibrated ordinary-visibility interval.
